_doc: Market folk: cultivators who live by trade and craft in the cities and markets (merchants, alchemists, healers, formation masters for hire, talisman sellers, appraisers, brokers, moneylenders). Page: market-folk.md. Batch 1: tier A, the dead, and the tier B Kết Đan.

people.gloss: Vermilion and blue pigments; a painter's fame
people.role: The pill-seller of Vật Hoa Thị: a pigment-grinder's son who charges whatever he likes, and holder of the only map of the Peach Spring
people.appearance: A round, cheerful man with vermilion under his fingernails that no washing removes, who wears a painter's smock over a silk robe worth a house.
people.backstory: Lạc Đan Thanh was born in 900 in Phong Sào Thôn on Cô Vụ Đảo, the son of a man who ground cinnabar and azurite for the island's painters. He learned fire from the mortar: cinnabar heated wrong turns to quicksilver and poisons the grinder, and that is how his father died. At twenty he sold the last of his father's pigments to a loose alchemist in Hạc Đinh Thị and stayed to keep his furnace. He has bought every method he uses, the Red Sun Scripture among them, and has never served a sect. In 1105 he paid Phan Vật Hoa (phan_vat_hoa) for the Peach Spring Painting at the season auction with a pill no one else could make (C183): the Vermilion-Azure Pill, ground like paint and fired like a pigment. In 1110 he opened his stall in Vật Hoa Thị on her ground and began charging whatever he likes (A186). He sells to every sect and to its enemies. Tăng Vân Tiêu (tang_van_tieu) owes him for three failed breakthrough pills. Vi Ngưng Yên (vi_ngung_yen) bought a dusk herb at his stall the year she died (N-yen_quang-02). His agents buy Thúy Vi's pills from Đậu Tam Thất (dau_tam_that) and copy the seals, and Úy Thanh Diễm (uy_thanh_diem) has not forgiven it. Hoa Cái Đường and half the west have asked for his recipes. He has sold none.
people.wants: To go into the Peach Spring when it opens in 1200 and come out remembering the way; failing that, to sell the painting for more than any lot has ever fetched at Vật Hoa Thị.
people.secret: He has been inside Đào Nguyên Cảnh once, at the opening of 1120, and came out with three peach stones and no memory of the road, as everyone does. The pill that made his name after 1120 is ground from those kernels, and one stone is left. His ledger of 1150 shows that Vi Ngưng Yên asked for the dusk herb by name, and that he wrote a warning beside the sale. He has never shown it, because it would clear him and shame her. The breakthrough pills he sells to cultivators who have already failed once hold a soul thread he buys each year from Hám Tàn Chung (ham_tan_chung) in the same market as the apricot clinic.

people.role: Healer of Hạnh Hoa Thị, the apricot-blossom market: cures what the alchemists of three sects will not touch
people.appearance: Small and plain, in a robe the colour of apricot blossom gone brown, with a roll of needles at her hip and lips faintly blue.
people.backstory: Giả Hồi Xuân was born in 1020 in Hạnh Hoa Thị, the market that grew below Thính Vũ's southern road (A290, A294), to a family that sold apricot blossom after rain. The old healer Mẫn Tế Thế (man_te_the) kept a clinic under the market's largest apricot tree and took her at seven to grind roots. The abbess Dương Hảo Vũ (duong_hao_vu) of Cốc Vũ Quán was the clinic's friend and had held her as a baby, and the two of them have traded herbs and hard cases all her life. When Mẫn died in 1110 (N-market_folk-04) she kept the clinic and the tree and did not raise her prices. Her fame is for the cases sect alchemists refuse: the poisons Ô Thiềm Tử (o_thiem_tu) sends her from the Night Rain Market, the lightning burns of the Tower's storm drills, the blind boy Ung Thính Thiền (ung_thinh_thien), whose eyes she tried and told him honestly why she could not mend. Bồ Ngọc Châm (bo_ngoc_cham) learned her salves at the clinic, Lam Nhuận Chi (lam_nhuan_chi) walks the hard cases down the road, and Dư Tục Đoạn (du_tuc_doan) of Thúy Vi trades cases with her by letter. Hoa Cái Đường has asked for her recipes. She gives them to anyone who will sit with a patient for a season, and no one from Hoa Cái has come.
people.wants: To leave the clinic and the tree to Nhiêu Tử Uyển (nhieu_tu_uyen), and to teach her to cure without tasting.
people.secret: She learns each new poison Ô Thiềm Tử sends by tasting it first. A hundred and fifty years of them sit in her meridians, held down by her own needles, and that is why her lips are blue. She has perhaps forty years left, not three hundred, and has told only the abbess. She also knows how to wake the gardener Tề Vong Quy (te_vong_quy) and has not done it: his daughter asked, and his mistress did not.

people.role: The richest merchant of the western plains: wool, wine, hulls and other people's debts, out of Nhạn Thanh Thành
people.appearance: A big, laughing man in plain wool with one gold coin on a cord at his throat, who remembers the name of every herder's child on the plain.
people.backstory: Kim Vạn Lý was born in 850 at the red-gold diggings of Xích Kim Khoáng above Vật Hoa Thị, where his father carried ore for Thiên Bảo Trai's furnaces. He left the mine at twelve with a sack of tailings and sold it twice. By a hundred and fifty he was the wool broker of the steppe. In 1002 he sold his share of Kim Cốc Viên's notes to the banker Quản Doanh Hư (quan_doanh_hu) a month before the garden crashed and Kim Cốc Thành burned (C174, N-market_folk-01). In 1040 he bought the wool of the whole plain in one season and became the richest merchant of the west (A170). His son Kim Tích Phúc (kim_tich_phuc) runs the caravans, and his grandson Kim Đắc Lộc (kim_dac_loc) is in Mục Vân Trang's stables. He owes everyone a little: Khúc Liệt Dương (khuc_liet_duong) a year's pay, Nhạc Thuần Nhưỡng (nhac_thuan_nhuong) forty jars of pure spring wine, the Pivot's treasury forty years of silver tolls. Diêm Hải Tảo (diem_hai_tao) owes him three hulls he never asks back. He buys Lạc Hà's notes from Thiên Bảo for Trầm Tịch Dương (tram_tich_duong), keeps a table at which Tiền Ngũ Phân (tien_ngu_phan) loses, and at every festival bets on Khấu Mục Vân's (khau_muc_van) horses against Tô Vãn Chiếu (to_van_chieu), and loses anyway (A172).
people.wants: To hand Kim Tích Phúc a house that does not need its founder, and to be buried with more owed to him than he owes.
people.secret: Since the cold year of 1120 (A171) killed the herds he had paid for, the house has run on credit from Từ Bỉnh Quyền (tu_binh_quyen) of Thiên Quyền Thị. He pays no debt until it is called. The lost bets are the one payment he never delays: losing to a sect head at her own festival is a gift no treasurer can call a bribe, and it buys the patience of everyone who could call his loans. Trầm's money sits in his hands for months between purchases, and he has used it to cover his own payments, though he has never yet failed to pass it on.

people.gloss: Letters and the loom of fate
people.role: A formation master for hire out of Tinh Hán Thành; Củng Tinh Quán's runaway, who sells the abbey's craft by the stone
people.appearance: Thin and stooped from a life bent over stones, in sand-coloured robes, with a habit of drawing figures in any dust he sits beside.
people.backstory: Vệ Văn Cơ was born in 980 in Tinh Hán Thành and drew formations in the harbour sand before he could talk (A230). A Củng Tinh Daoist buying lamp oil on the quay saw the figures, and the head Thẩm Bắc Thần (tham_bac_than) took the boy up to the plateau. He learned the stars and the Armillary Array Canon, and he learned that the abbey would sooner read the sky than lay a ward for a granary. In 1100 he left to lay formations for hire (N-cung_tinh-02). He has worked for anyone who pays: the Pivot's boundary steles, which he took twice from Phó Cương Đẩu (pho_cuong_dau) by bidding under the abbey; the Cloud Bridge Array, whose design he sold to Lạc Hà's Quách Tiếp Vân (quach_tiep_van) in 1180 (N-lac_ha-04); granary rings and caravan camps from the steppe to the coast. Thiện Thừa Củ (thien_thua_cu) offered him a place in the Pivot's Thiên Cơ Hall, and he turned it down, which the hall has not forgotten. In 1198 Quý Thủ Lũy (quy_thu_luy) paid him to re-lay the wards around the Vạn Cốt Trủng, and he quit after one night (A218) and gave back half the fee without saying why. He keeps two apprentices, both harbour children like himself.
people.wants: To be paid for the Cloud Bridge's outer ring, and to stand once more in Củng Tinh's armillary hall before he dies.
people.secret: The old wards around the Vạn Cốt Trủng are written in Củng Tinh's star-script, and their cornerstone carries his master's mark from 806: Thẩm Bắc Thần laid the barrow's wards for the Pivot after the war. They are failing on the side that faces the old field. Vệ would not be paid to unmake his master's work, and he has not written to ask why it was laid the way it was.

people.role: Mistress of the Từ counting house in Thiên Quyền Thị: the lender sects go to when they cannot be seen borrowing from Thiên Bảo
people.appearance: Grey-haired and straight-backed, in black, with a brass steelyard weight on a cord at her wrist; she counts while she listens.
people.backstory: Từ Bỉnh Quyền was born in 1010 above her father's weighing booth in Thiên Quyền Thị, the market of fair weights beside the Pivot's seat (A207). Six years before, her father had spent the house's savings on one of the four copies of Kim Cốc Viên's Golden Valley Ledger Canon that the ruined banker Quản Doanh Hư (quan_doanh_hu) sold in Vật Hoa Thị to pay his creditors (N-market_folk-02), so that his children would cultivate like merchants and not like sect servants. She opened it at nine. At thirty she lent her first hundred stones, to a Pivot outer disciple who wanted a better sword, and was repaid. The Từ house now lends to the vassals and small sects of the heartland and to elders who cannot be seen borrowing from Thiên Bảo Trai. Its one rule is that it never says who owes it. Each spring she has her weights checked against the Pivot's standard by Đặng Quân Bình (dang_quan_binh), who has never found them light. Since the cold year (A171) she has carried Kim Vạn Lý (kim_van_ly), and twice since 1180 Phan Vật Hoa (phan_vat_hoa) has offered to buy his paper from her.
people.wants: To have the Từ weights accepted by the Pivot as its own standard, so that her house never needs a lord's protection.
people.secret: She holds enough of Kim Vạn Lý's paper to own the Bào yards and the wool road by autumn if she called it. She will not. She has read in his books what his lost bets buy, and a merchant who can make a sect head grateful is worth more standing than fallen. She has also offered Đặng Quân Bình half the face of Kim's forty years of unpaid tolls, and Đặng has not answered.

people.role: Master of the Bào ship-house at Yên Ba Thành, builder of the cape's merchant hulls
people.appearance: Broad, bald and salt-burned, with one shoulder lower than the other since a mast fell on it in 1130; he smells of pine tar.
people.backstory: Bào Tế Hải was born in 1042 at Bạch Sa Trấn, two years after the Hỗ captain's Thẩm marriage and his jetty made the white sands a trading town (A029). His father Bào Thừa Phong (bao_thua_phong) came for the jetty, built coasting junks on the beach and sold them up and down the cape, most of them to the Hỗ fleet that Hỗ Tế Xuyên (ho_te_xuyen) now runs. The son built the first deep-keeled hull of Yên Ba and moved the yards into the city's harbour. In 1150 he paid the price of four hulls at Phan Vật Hoa's (phan_vat_hoa) season auction for the Still Moon Tide Scripture, and reached Kết Đan on it at a hundred and twenty. When his father died in 1160 (N-market_folk-05) the house was in debt for the new yards, and Kim Vạn Lý (kim_van_ly) paid it off for a third of the house. Bào builds the hulls Kim lends to Diêm Hải Tảo (diem_hai_tao) of Thúy Vi's port house, and drinks with her on their decks. His shipwright Quan Liêm Chu (quan_liem_chu) has shaped every keel since 1180. His daughter Bào Thính Triều (bao_thinh_trieu) wants to sail with Diêm wherever she goes.
people.wants: To build a hull that sails to the southern islands and comes back, which no ship of Yên Ba has done since Cô Phàm Các's fleet was lost in 705.
people.secret: In 1190 Kim Vạn Lý ordered the three hulls for Diêm deep-keeled and copper-sheathed for southern water, which means Kim knows she has a chart of the southern islands. Bào has not told her, because he wants to be on the ship when she sails it.

people.role: Debt broker of Ngũ Cốc Thành who buys bad paper at a tenth; granddaughter of the banker ruined in 1003
people.appearance: A narrow woman in mended grey who writes with her left hand and never sits with her back to a door.
people.backstory: Quản Phục Thu was born in 1125 in Ngũ Cốc Thành, the city that grew rich on the trade Kim Cốc lost (C176), into the family that lost the most. Her grandfather Quản Doanh Hư (quan_doanh_hu) had lent Kim Cốc Viên its last year of credit against its manuals, and in 1002 he bought Kim Vạn Lý's (kim_van_ly) share of its notes, a month before the crash (N-market_folk-01). When Kim Cốc Thành burned (C174) he sold four copies of the Golden Valley Ledger Canon to pay his creditors (N-market_folk-02), paid eighty parts in a hundred, and died. Market custom closes a dead man's ledger. In 1150 she opened it (N-market_folk-06), and took on its last twenty parts. She has paid them down for fifty years by buying bad debts at a tenth and collecting them in full, and her name is spat in four markets. Her brother Quản Thận Ngôn (quan_than_ngon) keeps Kim Vạn Lý's books. Tiền Ngũ Phân (tien_ngu_phan), the grandson of another Kim Cốc ruin, drinks with her after the auction.
people.wants: To close her grandfather's ledger paid in full, to buy back the four copies of the canon, and to see Kim Vạn Lý owe a debt he cannot pay.
people.secret: Her brother copies Kim's ledgers for her every new moon. She knows the house runs on Từ Bỉnh Quyền's credit. She has been offering to buy the small debts Kim leaves unpaid, Khúc Liệt Dương's year's wages and Nhạc's forty jars among them, so that she can call them all on one day and make Từ choose.

people.role: Appraiser of Thiều Âm Thị: bronze, bells and the old instruments the south ploughs up
people.appearance: Tall, with long ears weighted by bronze rings; she taps every object handed to her with a fingernail before she looks at it.
people.backstory: Born in 1060 among the instrument stalls of Thiều Âm Thị, the market of the Shao music that Phượng Minh's founder opened (A238), Liêu Thính Kim can name a bronze's foundry and century by the note it gives. She appraises what the farmers of Thê Ngô Lĩnh plough up from Cửu Thiều Cung's age for a tenth of the price, and Vưu Cẩm Thư (vuu_cam_thu) buys most of it for the palace's Hall of Spoils. She worked three seasons on Thiên Bảo's auction floor as a hired hand and left before Phan Vật Hoa (phan_vat_hoa) could make her an offer.

He opened a stall at Đào Sa Thị and sold wards to the river boats at half the hall's price. In 1173 Lạc Hà's raiders burned Lãng Đào's boats at Đào Sa with fire talismans painted at Nam Phố (A080, N-nam_pho-03), and his stall burned with them.
